reader.requirement: At --std 85 INITIALIZE must treat literal-1 (figurative constants included) and identifier-2 (elementary, group, signed, or an alphanumeric function-identifier) as sending operands that are only read, and each identifier-1 (subscripted or reference-modified included) as the receiving area, refusing an identifier-1 that cannot be a receiving operand (a literal, a function-identifier).

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 a numeric or integer function-identifier written as identifier-2 is refused (numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002, COBOL0900, §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4); an alphanumeric function stays legal

reader.edition-search: grep of Edition/Construct/Version in InitializeBinder.cs (only a comment naming the version pass for the 2002 phrases) and in ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving/ReceivingPlaceBar (only the error sink): the sending/receiving split itself consults no edition; identifier-1 is the grammar's receivingIdentifier at every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: a numeric or integer function-identifier as identifier-2 is refused at 85 (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4) and accepted at 2023 (ini3 prints [0005]); the sending/receiving roles themselves are the same
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness checks that elementary identifier-2 senders are left intact and literals are sent; it does not exercise a group sender, a signed sender, figurative constants, a subscripted or reference-modified identifier-1, a function-identifier sender, or the refusal of a non-receiving identifier-1

probes.expected: §1985:VI.6.17.3 SR1 with GR2/GR5: senders unchanged, each receiving elementary item gets the implicit MOVE (group-to-alphanumeric, -7 into PIC 99 is 07, ZERO/ALL "*", ref-mod receiver set to spaces)

probes.printed: COBOL5506 at INITIALIZE "AB" (no literal expected) and at INITIALIZE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(G-X) (expected a user-defined word), exit 65
probes.expected: identifier-1 is the receiving area, and §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR3a bars a function-identifier as a receiving operand

probes.printed: --std 85: COBOL0900 numeric or integer function-identifier ... requires COBOL-2002 (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4); --std 2023: [0005]
probes.expected: §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4: an integer function may be used only in an arithmetic expression, so it is no identifier-2 at 85

reader.notes: identifier-1 is the grammar's receivingIdentifier and resolves through the one receiving funnel ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving; identifier-2 binds through MoveBinder.SendingOperand and literal-1 through NullAdmittingOperand, so the roles are structural. The only edition arm on the path is the 1985 refusal of a numeric function as identifier-2, which is correct for 1985 (Amendment 1's SR4).

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.6.17.3 SR1-SR6 and VI.6.17.4 GR2-GR7, and VII.1.3.7 (LINAGE-COUNTER). Probes at --std 85: in1.cob INITIALIZE K E (K) REPLACING NUMERIC DATA BY 2 printed K=2 T=020 (E(2) set: subscript of the second receiving operand evaluated after K was set, GR6 left-to-right series of MOVEs); group sender G and signed sender G2 left unchanged ([AB][-012]) with receivers [AB01K][012]; ALL "XY" sender gives [XYXYX]. in2.cob INITIALIZE LINAGE-COUNTER refused COBOL2026 (a receiving operand only the I-O control system may change). in3.cob INITIALIZE ZERO refused COBOL5506. in4.cob FUNCTION LENGTH (X) as identifier-2 refused COBOL0900 at 85. INITIALIZE X REPLACING NUMERIC BY X (GR7 undefined overlap) accepted, which the text permits. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.17.3 SR1; OK §1985:VI.6.17.4 GR6; OK §1985:VII.1.3.7.
